# Glossary

    Edits to
    [`GLOSSARY.md`](https://github.com/batyanight/assaywatch/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md)

The project's own vocabulary. Use these words, exactly, in function and variable names,
comments, commit messages and conversation. Definitions are taken from `config.yaml`,
`assaywatch/schema.py` and module docstrings; the location is given where the repo defines
the term precisely. PCR basics are not defined here. Add a term here before inventing a new
word for a concept.

## Registry and assays

**assay**{: #term-assay } — one registry entry: one published [primer](#term-primer) set (plus optional [probe](#term-probe)) with its [target](#term-target), [chemistry](#term-chemistry) and [citation](#term-citation), stored as one YAML in `registry/` (`schema.py` `Assay`).

**oligo**{: #term-oligo } — any single oligonucleotide of an [assay](#term-assay): forward [primer](#term-primer), reverse primer, [probe](#term-probe) or an alternate (`schema.py` `Oligo`).

**primer**{: #term-primer } — a forward or reverse [oligo](#term-oligo); scored by its distance from the 3' end.

**probe**{: #term-probe } — the internal [oligo](#term-oligo) of a `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb` or `lna` [assay](#term-assay); absent in `conventional`, `sybr` and `rpa` assays, so 158 of 218 entries have none (`assaywatch validate registry` prints the split; `config.yaml scoring:` for how a probe is scored).

**chemistry**{: #term-chemistry } — the [assay](#term-assay)'s [detection](#term-detection) format, one of `conventional`, `sybr`, `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb`, `lna`, `rpa`; scoring overrides are keyed on it (`schema.py` `Chemistry`, `config.yaml scoring: by_chemistry`).

**amplicon**{: #term-amplicon } — the product between the facing forward and reverse sites in a record.

**amplicon_bp**{: #term-amplicon-bp } — the [amplicon](#term-amplicon) length in bp, measured from where the primers sit on real GenBank records, never copied from the paper (`CLAUDE.md` "Measure, never quote").

**amplicon_bp_range**{: #term-amplicon-bp-range } — `[min, max]` declared for an [assay](#term-assay) whose product length genuinely varies by species; mutually exclusive with `amplicon_bp` (`schema.py`).

**species_sizes**{: #term-species-sizes } — measured product length per species, only valid alongside `amplicon_bp_range` (`schema.py` `SpeciesSize`).

**amplicon_disagrees_with_paper**{: #term-amplicon-disagrees-with-paper } — [review flag](#term-review-flag): the measured [amplicon](#term-amplicon) length differs from the published one, and the registry keeps the measured value (`CLAUDE.md`, `review.py`).

**target**{: #term-target } — what the [assay](#term-assay) is for: `taxid`, `taxon_name`, `gene`, `genome_type`, optional `query` (`schema.py` `Target`).

**scope_taxids**{: #term-scope-taxids } — taxa the [assay](#term-assay) is meant to [detect](#term-detect); a record counts toward the [drift](#term-drift) denominator when its taxid or any ancestor is listed (`schema.py` `Target`, `config.yaml drift: scope_taxonomy`).

**exclusivity**{: #term-exclusivity } — a published claim that the [assay](#term-assay) does not amplify certain off-target taxa; those taxa are listed in `target.exclusivity_taxids`, retrieved on purpose, and reported as predicted cross-reactivity, never scored (`schema.py` `Target`).

**citation**{: #term-citation } — the paper an entry rests on (`schema.py` `Citation`); every live entry cites its own paper.

**doi_verified**{: #term-doi-verified } — `true` only after `scripts/resolve_citations.py` and `scripts/check_citations.py` have confirmed the DOI against Crossref; a DOI is always entered as `false` first (`CLAUDE.md`).

**status (active, draft, deprecated)**{: #term-status } — registry lifecycle; only a maintainer sets `active`, and an entry in `registry/` must also carry `doi_verified: true` (`schema.py` `Status`).

**pending entry**{: #term-pending-entry } — an [assay](#term-assay) YAML waiting for a verified DOI; it sits in `pending/`, is never screened, and is checked with `python -m assaywatch.validate pending --pending` (`CLAUDE.md`).

**review flag (needs_review)**{: #term-review-flag } — a controlled-vocabulary tag on an entry that can be filtered on, e.g. `oligos_read_from_figure`, `not_screenable`, `thin_evidence`; the specifics of one case go in prose, not the [flag](#term-flag) (`review.py`).

**nested protocol**{: #term-nested-protocol } — a nested or semi-nested protocol, stored as one entry per round, each screened as an independent [assay](#term-assay) and then cross-warned (`nested.py`).

**conditions**{: #term-conditions } — the thermal and reagent protocol exactly as the paper prints it (annealing temperature, salts, [oligo](#term-oligo) concentrations, `master_mix`); nothing in it is screened (`schema.py` `Conditions`).

**master mix**{: #term-master-mix } — the commercial reaction mix named in the paper, stored as the free-text `Conditions.master_mix` field; keep the term, it is the reagent's name.

**performance**{: #term-performance } — what the paper measured (LOD, efficiency, R squared, dynamic range); reported, not scored (`schema.py` `Performance`).

**panel**{: #term-panel } — one inclusivity or [exclusivity](#term-exclusivity) validation panel the paper ran, as counts `n_tested` and `n_detected` (`schema.py` `Panel`).

**use_context**{: #term-use-context } — free-text list of the settings an [assay](#term-assay) is used in; the intended use that the `drift.detect_fraction_threshold` comment says the right threshold depends on.

## Screening and scoring

**screen**{: #term-screen } — match every [oligo](#term-oligo) of an [assay](#term-assay) against every record of an [archive](#term-archive) and write one [call](#term-call) per (assay, record) (`screen.py`).

**call**{: #term-call } — the per-record outcome of a [screen](#term-screen) for one [assay](#term-assay), one of `detect`, `reduced`, `fail`, `indeterminate`, `no_amplicon` (`score.py` `Call`).

**detect**{: #term-detect } — a [call](#term-call): the summed [penalty](#term-penalty) is at most `scoring.detect_max` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**reduced**{: #term-reduced } — a [call](#term-call): amplifies but with [penalty](#term-penalty) above `detect_max` and at most `reduced_max`; [drift](#term-drift) counts it as detected unless the [assay](#term-assay)'s [chemistry](#term-chemistry) is in `drift.reduced_not_detected_for` (`config.yaml`).

**fail**{: #term-fail } — a [call](#term-call): both primers land but the [penalty](#term-penalty) exceeds `reduced_max`, or a [terminal mismatch](#term-terminal-mismatch) fails it (`terminal_mismatch_fails`).

**no_amplicon**{: #term-no-amplicon } — a [call](#term-call): no facing [primer](#term-primer) pair in the right orientation within the [amplicon](#term-amplicon) size range; kept out of the [drift](#term-drift) fraction (`drift.py`, `score.py`).

**indeterminate**{: #term-indeterminate } — a [call](#term-call): too many undetermined record bases (ambiguity codes, N) under an [oligo](#term-oligo) to score; kept out of the [drift](#term-drift) fraction (`score.py`).

**detection**{: #term-detection } — the predicted outcome that a record would amplify, i.e. a `detect` or (unless excluded) `reduced` [call](#term-call); [drift](#term-drift)'s numerator is the detected share.

**not detected**{: #term-not-detected } — a `reduced` [call](#term-call) counted as not detected for the chemistries in `drift.reduced_not_detected_for` (currently `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb`), where a [reduced](#term-reduced) [probe](#term-probe) call stops counting as a find (`config.yaml drift:`).

**evaluable record**{: #term-evaluable-record } — a record with a `detect`, `reduced` or `fail` [call](#term-call); the only records in the [drift](#term-drift) denominator (`drift.py`).

**exclusion**{: #term-exclusion } — the reason a record yielded no [amplicon](#term-amplicon): `no_site`, `truncated`, `diverged`, `no_pair`, or `chance_only` (`score.py classify_exclusion`).

**site**{: #term-site } — a position in a record where an [oligo](#term-oligo) binds with at most `max_mismatches_searched` mismatches, found on both strands (`match.py`).

**penalty**{: #term-penalty } — the position-weighted mismatch cost of one [oligo](#term-oligo); forward, reverse and [probe](#term-probe) penalties are summed into one budget under the shipped `engine: budget` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**3' window**{: #term-3-window } — the last `primer_3prime_window` (5) nt at a [primer](#term-primer)'s 3' end, penalized by `primer_3prime_penalty` per mismatch (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**mid window**{: #term-mid-window } — positions 6 to 10 from the 3' end, penalized by `primer_mid_penalty` per mismatch (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**5' region**{: #term-5-region } — the rest of a [primer](#term-primer), penalized by `primer_5prime_penalty` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**terminal mismatch**{: #term-terminal-mismatch } — a mismatch at the 3'-most base of a [primer](#term-primer); with `terminal_mismatch_fails: true` it makes the [call](#term-call) `fail` regardless of identity (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**mispair**{: #term-mispair } — the identity of a mismatch (template base : [primer](#term-primer) base, e.g. `G:T`), as opposed to its position; `mispair_penalty` overrides the cost of named mispairs such as G:T wobble (`config.yaml scoring:`, `score.py`).

**mispair window**{: #term-mispair-window } — how many bases from the 3' end `mispair_penalty` applies; null means `primer_3prime_window` (`scoring.mispair_window`).

**engine (budget, serial)**{: #term-engine } — how [oligo](#term-oligo) penalties combine: `budget` sums them against `detect_max`/`reduced_max`; `serial` judges each oligo alone and the worst decides (`scoring.engine`).

**degeneracy**{: #term-degeneracy } — the pool size of a degenerate [oligo](#term-oligo) (product of its ambiguity-code multiplicities); reported with `tiers` negligible, moderate, high, never penalized (`degeneracy.py`, `config.yaml degeneracy:`).

**degenerate base**{: #term-degenerate-base } — an IUPAC ambiguity code written in an [oligo](#term-oligo), synthesised as a mixture; inosine is kept in `seq_as_written` (`iupac.py`, `schema.py`).

**ambiguous (record base)**{: #term-ambiguous } — a record position whose true base is undetermined; reported separately and never scored as a mismatch (`match.py`).

**chance pair**{: #term-chance-pair } — a forward and reverse [site](#term-site) that face each other in [amplicon](#term-amplicon) range by chance in a long record, with nothing to do with the [target](#term-target) (`chance.py`).

**E-value (site, pair)**{: #term-e-value } — expected number of such sites or pairs by chance in a record of that length and composition; `max_site_evalue` and `max_pair_evalue` set the credibility cut (`chance.py`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**locus identity**{: #term-locus-identity } — whether an [amplicon](#term-amplicon)'s interior resembles the interiors of the amplicons the [assay](#term-assay) actually works on, the chemistry-independent form of the probe-site test; shipped off (`locus_identity_min: null`) (`locus_identity.py`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**thermo**{: #term-thermo } — optional nearest-neighbor duplex Tm and delta Tm columns per [oligo](#term-oligo); shown, never scored, shipped `thermo: false` (`thermo.py`, `config.yaml`).

**footprint**{: #term-footprint } — one record's mismatch pattern for an [assay](#term-assay) (positions from the 3' end and ambiguity counts per [oligo](#term-oligo)), interned to a single string; millions of records share a few thousand footprints (`drift.py FOOTPRINT_COLUMNS`, `calls.py`).

**strategy**{: #term-strategy } — a pre-registered candidate scoring change, one YAML in `strategies/` overriding `config.yaml` values and carrying its own kill criterion, replayed against frozen sets.

**S-ladder (S0, S3b, S7, ...)**{: #term-s-ladder } — the numbered ladder of candidate scoring strategies; `S0` is the shipped rule, names are reserved in `docs/journal/2026-10-24-scoring-strategy-test-plan.md` (S5 is C2, the gated Bayesian per-record model) (`ROADMAP.md`).

## Drift and verdicts

**drift**{: #term-drift } — a fall over time in the share of GenBank records for a taxon in which an [assay](#term-assay)'s oligos still match; not the same as loss of infections detected (`config.yaml` "WHAT DRIFT IS AND IS NOT").

**baseline**{: #term-baseline } — the pooled earlier records an [assay](#term-assay)'s [recent window](#term-recent-window) is contrasted with (`drift.py`).

**deposit date**{: #term-deposit-date } — the day a record first appeared in GenBank (`created` in the metadata; esummary `CreateDate`, or an [assembly](#term-assembly)'s `release_date`); the clock every verdict, window and [trend](#term-trend) runs on (`calls.read_dates`).

**collection date**{: #term-collection-date } — the day the isolate behind a record was collected, as BioSample gives it (a full date, a year-month, a bare year, a range or "missing"); carried for [assembly](#term-assembly) records only, in the `collected` metadata column and, for older archives, in the title (`assemblies.py`, `metadata.collection_year`).

**collection-year lens**{: #term-collection-year-lens } — the report section that re-dates each record by its collection YEAR and recomputes the recent share beside the deposit-clock one; a lens on sequencing backlog that moves no status (`report.collection_lens_rows`; decided 2026-10-30, `docs/journal/2026-10-30-design-grilled.md` Q1-Q3). [Assembly](#term-assembly) records only until `report.collection_sidecar` names the file `scripts/backfill_collection_dates.py` fetched; then every record.

**recent window**{: #term-recent-window } — the latest `recent_window_months` (24) of deposit dates, widened a year at a time up to `max_window_months` (60) when records are scarce (`config.yaml drift:`).

**status**{: #term-status-2 } — the per-assay [drift](#term-drift) verdict: `stable`, `watch`, `declining`, `low coverage`, `insufficient data` (`drift.py`, `README.md` "The drift [call](#term-call)").

**declining**{: #term-declining } — status: recent share is below `detect_fraction_threshold`, the fall is at least `min_decline` with a [Newcombe interval](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval) wholly below zero, and the [assay](#term-assay) cleared the threshold in some earlier year (`drift.require_working_baseline`) (`README.md`, `config.yaml drift:`).

**low coverage**{: #term-low-coverage } — status: below threshold but not measurably lower than before, or never working; an [assay](#term-assay) used beyond its design, or one that was always poor (`README.md`).

**watch**{: #term-watch } — status: below threshold with an interval that still covers it (`README.md`).

**insufficient data**{: #term-insufficient-data } — status: fewer than `min_records_for_drift` [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records; reported, never flagged (`config.yaml drift:`).

**flag**{: #term-flag } — in [drift](#term-drift), an [assay](#term-assay) whose recent upper [Wilson](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval) bound falls below the threshold (`flag_rule: wilson`) or whose posterior probability of being below it exceeds `flag_posterior_credibility` (`posterior`). Not a [review flag](#term-review-flag).

**detect_fraction_threshold**{: #term-detect-fraction-threshold } — share below which an [assay](#term-assay) is called failing, 0.90; a judgement about tolerable surveillance loss (`config.yaml drift:`).

**lineage**{: #term-lineage } — a group of records of one [assay](#term-assay)'s [target](#term-target) defined by NCBI taxid (grouped at `group_at_rank: species`), so a miss on one clade is not averaged away (`lineage.py`, `config.yaml lineage:`).

**sublineage**{: #term-sublineage } — a finer split within one taxid, resolved from titles or by sequence-homology clustering (`cluster`, Mode C) where the taxid carries no label (`subcluster.py`, `clustermaps.py`, `config.yaml lineage: sublineage`).

**lineage-conditional verdict**{: #term-lineage-conditional-verdict } — the assay-level verdict overridden when any one [lineage](#term-lineage) is significantly below threshold after Holm correction (`lineage.multiple_testing`), so the worst lineage drives the [call](#term-call) (`lineage.py`, `config.yaml lineage:`).

**site drift**{: #term-site-drift } — which [oligo](#term-oligo) positions are failing and in which [footprint](#term-footprint) groups of accessions, for assays the main report calls [declining](#term-declining) (`sitedrift.py`).

**trend**{: #term-trend } — a Cochran-Armitage test for a monotone slide in the detected share by deposit year, reported beside the verdict, never folded into it (`trend.py`, `config.yaml drift: trend_min_years`). Printed twice since 2026-10-30: by record (an upper bound on the evidence, since duplicated deposits count as independent) and **by [footprint](#term-footprint)** (each distinct footprint counted once per year; nearer a lower bound, since a sequencing error in a [primer](#term-primer) [site](#term-site) mints a footprint). When they disagree on direction the report says so.

**hierarchical layer (C1)**{: #term-hierarchical-layer } — Beta-binomial partial pooling of an [assay](#term-assay)'s lineages; reported, never a verdict unless `verdict_from: posterior` (`hierarchical.py`).

**Wilson / Newcombe interval**{: #term-wilson-newcombe-interval } — Wilson score interval for a proportion; Newcombe hybrid-score interval for a difference of two, built from the two Wilson intervals (`interval.py`, `drift.py`).

## Pipeline and runs

**retrieve**{: #term-retrieve } — fetch nucleotide records for a [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group) from NCBI and [archive](#term-archive) them, incrementally (`retrieve.py`).

**retrieval group**{: #term-retrieval-group } — a (taxid, `target.query`) pair; assays sharing both share one [archive](#term-archive), on disk at `data/retrieved/<taxid>/<slug>/` (`retrieve.py`, `groups.py`).

**archive**{: #term-archive } — the gzipped FASTA plus `*.meta.tsv.gz` for one [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group), keeping whole records so rescreening at any setting is free (`windows.py`, `retrieve.py`).

**assembly (`asm` group)**{: #term-assembly } — a [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group) of sampled bacterial genome assemblies (`assemblies.taxa`, `per_year`) cut down to the loci the oligos could build an [amplicon](#term-amplicon) in, used where gene-level deposits stopped (`assemblies.py`).

**window archive**{: #term-window-archive } — an [archive](#term-archive) cut down to a `buffer_bp` window around the sites a [screen](#term-screen) found, for distribution (`windows.py`).

**manifest**{: #term-manifest } — the [retrieve](#term-retrieve) stage's run state: per-group last-run dates and counts, kept as state not as a Snakemake output (`retrieve.py`, `timing.py`).

**run record**{: #term-run-record } — what `retrieve` returns for one fetched group (`TaxonRun`), written to the [manifest](#term-manifest) (`retrieve.py`).

**screen signature**{: #term-screen-signature } — the record, written beside a cached [screen](#term-screen), of what it was produced under, so `collect` can [detect](#term-detect) a stale screen whatever Snakemake remembers (`signature.py`).

**rescreen**{: #term-rescreen } — re-run `screen_archive` over the archives after a scoring or code change; the shipped scoring hash forces one (`config.yaml scoring:`, `signature.py`).

**collect**{: #term-collect } — gather the cached per-archive screens into one [calls table](#term-calls-table), `calls.tsv.gz` (`collect.py`).

**calls table**{: #term-calls-table } — `results/<date>/calls.tsv.gz`, one row per ([assay](#term-assay), record) (`calls.py`).

**taxa cache**{: #term-taxa-cache } — `docs/taxa-cache.json`, the [lineage](#term-lineage) analysis's taxid-to-name map (`config.yaml lineage.taxa_cache`); not the taxon records.

**taxon record**{: #term-taxon-record } — an entry in `docs/taxon-records.cache.json`: NCBI scientific name, common name and rank for a taxid, used by the [assay](#term-assay) sheet (`docs/assay-sheet.md`).

**pipeline stages**{: #term-pipeline-stages } — Snakefile rules `validate`, `retrieve`, `screen_archive`, `collect_calls`, `report`, `site_drift`, `lineage_analysis`, `degeneracy_table`, `figures`; `all` requests the outputs (`Snakefile`).

## Evidence and curation

**retrospective case**{: #term-retrospective-case } — a row in `docs/validation-cases*.tsv`: a published follow-up where an [assay](#term-assay) worked or failed, with its mechanism (`coverage` or `drift`); the evidence the thresholds are checked against (`config.yaml` header).

**development set**{: #term-development-set } — `docs/validation-cases.tsv`, the cases thresholds were tuned against, so figures on it are in-sample (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**held-out set**{: #term-held-out-set } — validation cases reserved for one decision and not consulted for any threshold; `validation-cases-heldout.tsv` is spent, `-heldout-2.tsv` is current (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**bench panel**{: #term-bench-panel } — a per-strain wet-lab result table read from a paper into `docs/bench-panels/*.tsv`, used as sensitivity and specificity evidence for scoring changes (`docs/INDEX.md`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**design era**{: #term-design-era } — how much sequence existed when an [assay](#term-assay) was designed versus now (`records_before_design`, `records_now`, fold increase), from `scripts/design_era.py` into `docs/design-era.tsv` (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**predict protocol**{: #term-predict-protocol } — `source.predict_protocol`, the `P-0nn` protocol under which an entry's oligos were extracted (`schema.py` `Source`).

## Resolved from the repo on 2026-10-29

**tier-2 (validation)**{: #term-tier-2 } — retrospective validation: assays with published follow-up (a paper, erratum or redesign reporting the [assay](#term-assay) failing or still working on particular lineages), asked whether AssayWatch flags what the literature found using only records deposited before that paper; scored as a confusion matrix with Jeffreys intervals by `scripts/retrospective.py` (`ROADMAP.md` "Tier 2: retrospective validation"). No tier-1 is named anywhere; the word survives from the original plan's numbering.

**ground truth**{: #term-ground-truth } — a documented outcome for an ([assay](#term-assay), [lineage](#term-lineage)) pair from a [tier-2](#term-tier-2) case or a [bench panel](#term-bench-panel) row; a [flag](#term-flag) with "no ground truth either way" is one no paper or [panel](#term-panel) has judged (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**evaluable / assessable / coverage gap**{: #term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap } — three thresholds on one count. A record is *evaluable* when both primers anchored in range so it received an [amplicon](#term-amplicon) (`config.yaml` under `chance_pair_fdr`). A [lineage](#term-lineage) is *assessable* when it has at least `lineage.min_records_per_lineage` evaluable records. A *coverage gap* is an assay-level shortfall below `drift.min_records_for_coverage`. Same denominator, three places it is tested.

**undecided**{: #term-undecided } — the set of [drift](#term-drift) statuses that are not a verdict: `insufficient data`, `no recent data`, `no data` (`scripts/retrospective.py UNDECIDED`). `drift.py STATUS_ORDER` carries the first two and `NO_DATA` the third; the report grays all three. `no recent data` means nothing new was deposited in the window; `insufficient data` means too few [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records; `no data` means no [archive](#term-archive) at all.

**C1 / C2 / C3**{: #term-c1-c2-c3 } — the three layers of `docs/bayesian-scoring-plan.md`: C1 the [drift](#term-drift) proportion (replaces [Wilson](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval)/Newcombe and the [flag](#term-flag) rule), C2 the per-record [call](#term-call) (replaces the additive [penalty](#term-penalty) table), C3 the validation matrix intervals (replaces point sensitivity). The **S ladder** (`docs/journal/2026-10-24-scoring-strategy-test-plan.md`, S0 [baseline](#term-baseline), S3b, S7, S7b…) is a sequence of candidate *scoring rules* inside C2's territory, each pre-registered with kill criteria. C-numbers name what is modeled; S-numbers name one tested change to the penalty rule.

**retrospective families**{: #term-retrospective-families } — the phrase families that `scripts/find_retrospective_cases.py` uses to find citing papers (`docs/journal/2026-10-26-retrospective-case-search.md`): `miss`, a paper reporting the [assay](#term-assay) missing samples (the scarce `fails` kind, or a clinical sensitivity report); `weakened`, [reduced](#term-reduced) or partial [detection](#term-detection); `mismatch`, a paper locating [primer](#term-primer) mismatches against a [lineage](#term-lineage) (the best route to a `drift` case); `redesign`, a group redesigning the assay, which usually says why; `use`, opt-in, a paper that simply uses the assay and so may test our oligos on new material (`docs/journal/2026-10-29-use-family-cases.md`); `late_redesign`, opt-in and pre-registered, a redesign published five or more years after the design paper, the first source tried for a `drift` case (`docs/journal/2026-10-30-redesign-family.md`).

**lineage Modes A, B, C**{: #term-lineage-modes-a-b-c } — the three ways a record is assigned to a [sublineage](#term-sublineage) (`assaywatch/lineage.py` docstrings). Mode A: by taxid, when NCBI already distinguishes the sublineages below the query taxon (Avipoxvirus: fowlpox vs canarypox). Mode B: by a title token regex (influenza subtype `(H5N1)`). Mode C: by a sequence cluster label from `assaywatch/subcluster.py` (Bd BdGPL vs BdCAPE). Each returns None to defer to the next.
